en.title: Transportation
en.goal: Ask how to get somewhere by public transport or taxi.
vocab: one ticket (张 is the measure word here)

phrases.t: How do you get to the airport?
I want to buy a ticket.

dialogue.title: Asking how to get somewhere
lines: How do you get to the airport?
You can take the subway or a taxi.

zenme.title: 怎么 (zěnme) — asking "how"
zenme.body: 怎么 (zěnme) asks about the way something is done, and usually comes before the verb — it's like "how" in English when you ask about the method or way of doing something.
examples: how do you get to the airport?

qu-lai.title: 去 (qù) and 来 (lái) — "go" and "come"
qu-lai.body: 去 (qù) means "to go" and is followed directly by the destination, with no preposition. 来 (lái) means "to come" — together, they are the two basic directional verbs in Chinese, showing movement away from or toward the speaker.

zoulu-vs-zuo.title: "Zǒu lù" or "zuò dìtiě"?
zoulu-vs-zuo.body: To go on foot, you just say zǒu lù (走路, to walk), with no other verb. For any vehicle you get into and sit in, you use zuò (坐, literally "to sit") before the means of transport — the same "zuò" as sitting on a chair; think of it as "to go sitting in".

zuo-chuzuche-dache.title: In everyday speech, "zuò chūzūchē" becomes "dǎchē"
zuo-chuzuche-dache.body: Instead of the full structure zuò chūzūchē (to go by taxi), the everyday verb for "taking a taxi" (or a ride-hailing car) is dǎchē (打车, literally "to hit a car") — used all the time instead of the longer phrase.
examples: to take a taxi / hail a car (everyday speech)
